The PKGBUILD fetches a prebuilt .deb package from the project's official GitHub Releases page using a direct HTTPS URL. The package() function extracts the contents of the .deb archive using standard bsdtar commands, which is a common and safe practice for binary packages in AUR. It then sets appropriate permissions on the chrome-sandbox binary (required for Electron apps) and creates a symlink in /usr/bin for system-wide access.

No suspicious commands such as curl, wget, eval, base64, or exec are present. There is no obfuscated code, network exfiltration, or execution of downloaded scripts. The operations performed are consistent with standard packaging practices for distributing a closed-source Electron application. While the pkgdesc mentions "stealth overlay that screen sharing cannot see", this describes the application's intended functionality — not malicious behavior in the packaging script. Such features are part of the upstream application and do not indicate a supply-chain compromise in the PKGBUILD itself.

The license, dependencies, and metadata are clearly defined and appropriate. All actions are confined to the build and package directories, with no attempts to modify system files outside of $pkgdir. The use of chmod 4755 on chrome-sandbox is standard for Electron-based applications to enable proper sandboxing at runtime.
</details>
